title: 1997 AMC 8 Problem 22

concepts.label: Power scaling of length, area, and volume

statement: A two-inch cube \((2\times 2\times 2)\) of silver weighs \(3\) pounds and is worth \(\$ 200.\) How much is a three-inch cube of silver worth?

solutions.text:
The two-inch cube consists of \(2^3 = 8\) unit cubes. Each of these unit cubes is worth \[ 200 \div 8 = 25 \] dollars. To form a three-inch cube, you need \(3^3 = 27\) unit cubes. This means that it is worth \[ 25 \cdot 27 = 675 \] dollars.

Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: Compare the numbers of unit cubes in the two cubes
